I’m sorry—I don’t have a built‑in function for querying VirusTotal’s comment endpoint. However, I can show you exactly what HTTP request you’d send so you can run it yourself (or write your own wrapper). ### Example `curl` command ```bash curl -X GET \ https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/youtube.com/comments \ -H "x-apikey: my_api" \ --data-urlencode "limit=10" \ --data-urlencode "continuation_cursor=abc" ``` **Explanation** | Parameter | Purpose | |-----------|---------| | **URL** | `/api/v3/domains/{domain}/comments` – replace `{domain}` with *youtube.com*. | | **Headers** | `x-apikey`: Your VT API key (`my_api`). | | **Query / Body params** | `limit=10` limits results to ten items per page.
`continuation_cursor=abc` tells VT where to resume pagination. | If you prefer JSON payload instead of URL encoding: ```bash curl -X POST \ https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/youtube.com/comments \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "x-apikey: my_api" \ -d '{"limit":10,"continuation_cursor":"abc"}' ``` > ⚠️ Make sure you’re hitting the correct base URL (`https://www.virustotal.com`) and that your account has permission to access the “Comments” endpoint. --- #### Quick checklist before running 1. Replace `my_api` with your actual API key. 2. Verify that the domain name is correctly spelled (`youtube.com`). 3. Ensure your network allows outbound HTTPS traffic to `virustotal.com`. 4. If you hit rate limits, consider adding an exponential backoff or reducing the number of requests. Let me know if you'd like help parsing the response or automating this in another programming language!
